tests.prompt: Our Shopify store has about 4,000 products. Before Black Friday, find the products with broken pages: missing photos, no description, $0 prices, fake sale prices. Don't change anything yet.
tests.good: Uses a read-only token with read_products only. Builds a cheap index by paginating products with lean fields (mediaCount, descriptionHtml, variant price and compareAtPrice, productType, vendor, status, publishedAt), pacing on throttleStatus and noting that variants(first: 100) truncates. Computes flags in code (0 or 1 image, description under about 20 characters, $0 variant, compare-at at or below price, missing type or vendor). Ranks clusters with a stated reason each, weighting active published products over drafts; deep-reads only that slice; verifies each finding on the Admin API, not the sitemap; states what was not checked. Proposes fixes through export, diff and confirmation, and writes nothing.

tests.prompt: We sell coffee filters and espresso machine parts. Here's a CSV of the last 120 days of sales by SKU and our stock count from last Monday. What should I reorder this week from each vendor?
tests.good: Maps the CSV columns back to the user; nets out sales since last Monday's count; asks once for lead times, pack sizes, minimums and units already on order. Computes 7- and 28-day velocity per variant excluding out-of-stock days and inspects any gap over 50%. Times stockouts on the higher rate, sizes on the 28-day rate with (60 + lead time) x v28 minus on hand and inbound, buffer min(30, max(7, lead/2)), pack rounding with a 90-day ceiling, MOQ checked per vendor order. Lists slow movers with cash tied up, skips seasonality (under 400 days) and asks instead, costs every line with vendor totals, and drafts no PO or email without approval.

tests.prompt: Add Stripe checkout to our custom Next.js store (products live in our own Postgres database). We ship physical goods to the US and EU and want a subscribe-and-save option on coffee beans.
tests.good: Uses Checkout Sessions with line items priced from the server-side catalog, no payment_method_types, shipping address collection and shipping options, promotion codes, and a stock re-check. Fulfils from checkout.session.completed and async_payment_succeeded gated on payment_status, and handles async failure, refunds and disputes. Subscriptions use mode subscription, one Product per plan, the Customer Portal and subscription and invoice event handlers. Stripe Tax: head office set, registrations the user confirms, automatic_tax enabled, a test calculation checked for not_collecting, tax codes from Stripe's list confirmed by the user, EU B2B tax id collection. Restricted keys; sandbox tests with a decline, 3-D Secure and a delayed payment.

tests.prompt: We're launching a skincare brand on Shopify next month. Import our 60 products from this spreadsheet, get them into Google Shopping with a campaign, and write product descriptions that don't sound generic. We also need clean white-background product photos from our phone shots.
tests.good: States a plan first: ecommerce catalog-and-feeds.md for the import (CSV template, one row per variant, Published FALSE, GTINs, export-diff-confirm) and the Google & YouTube channel feed (item_group_id, matching prices, disapprovals); content-creation conversion-copy.md for descriptions without health claims that trip Merchant Center policy; image-creation editing-references-consistency.md for white backgrounds that keep the real product unchanged; google-ads campaign-build.md for the Shopping campaign once the feed is approved. Publishes products only after the user confirms and checks the Done means of all four crafts.

tests.prompt: My Shopify store says 412 orders last month but GA4 shows only 331 purchases, and the revenue numbers are off too. I have the Shopify order export CSV and read access to the GA4 property (ID 481516234). Work out why they differ, tell me how much of the gap is normal and how much is a tracking bug, and tell me what to fix.
tests.good: Pulls GA4 with the Data API runReport (transactions or ecommercePurchases and purchaseRevenue by date and transactionId) under read-only scope, not by editing the property. Reconciles against the Shopify export on the same timezone and currency, after excluding test, cancelled, voided, refunded, POS and draft orders, and joins on order id to name the exact orders missing from GA4 and any duplicate transaction_id. Checks the usual causes: consent mode and ad blockers, thank-you page vs Customer Events pixel, a GA4 tag firing twice (Shopify's Google channel plus a pasted tag), payment-gateway redirects (PayPal, off-site checkouts) dropping the session or client_id, and API thresholding or sampling. Separates the expected small gap from a bug with sample counts and a stated threshold instead of guessing. States what could not be verified (consent rate, unsampled data) and changes no tags or settings without the owner's yes. Gives ordered, testable fixes (for example verify with GA4 DebugView on a test order).

tools.name: Shopify
tools.why: Leads the top-traffic tier (6.08% vs WooCommerce 3.12% of high-traffic sites, HTTP Archive May 2026, via GravityKit) and ~30% of US stores; has an official Claude merchant connector (May 2026) and Dev MCP.

tools.name: WooCommerce
tools.why: Most detected store platform on the web (6.64% of origins, HTTP Archive May 2026; ~35% of stores in GravityKit's roundup); ships a developer-preview MCP endpoint.

tools.name: Stripe
tools.why: Default payment API for custom and headless stores and named in 2026 stack round-ups (Shopify, Klaviyo, GA4, Stripe); official remote MCP and Claude connector.

tools.name: Google Merchant Center
tools.why: The feed that powers Shopping ads and free listings for nearly every store; Content API for Shopping was sunset on 18 Aug 2026 so Merchant API is now required (Google docs).

tools.name: Google Analytics 4
tools.why: Named as the standard analytics layer in 2026 ecommerce stack guides (Shopify, Klaviyo, GA4, Stripe); official Google MCP server has 3.4k stars.

tools.name: PayPal
tools.why: The second payment method on most stores after cards; official remote MCP at mcp.paypal.com and an Agent Toolkit (e-tailize official-MCP round-up, 2026).

tools.name: Wix eCommerce
tools.why: Second-largest platform on the measurable web (1.48%, HTTP Archive May 2026) and ~23% of US stores in the Mobiloud roundup; official Wix MCP is a built-in Claude connector.

tools.name: Amazon Seller Central
tools.why: Over 95% of independent sellers in Amazon's store sell on several channels and 71% of Amazon-primary sellers earn 75%+ of marketplace revenue there (Amazon, Sept 2026, via ppc.land); official SP-API MCP released.

tools.name: Squarespace Commerce
tools.why: 1.12% of measurable web and ~16% of US stores (HTTP Archive May 2026; Mobiloud); REST Commerce APIs for orders, products, inventory but no official MCP.

tools.name: BigCommerce
tools.why: Mid-market SaaS with ~$32B GMV (2.5% share) in the 2026 roundup though only 0.14% of web origins; Storefront MCP in early access.

tools.name: Adobe Commerce
tools.why: 0.38% of measurable web (HTTP Archive May 2026) and the incumbent in large B2B and enterprise catalogs.

tools.name: Square
tools.why: Common POS plus online store for small merchants and the usual path for omnichannel retail; official square-mcp-server (108 stars, Apache-2.0).

tools.name: Shippo
tools.why: Free up to 30 labels a month and an official OAuth MCP at mcp.shippo.com also in Claude's connector directory (Ringly 2026 shipping comparison, Shippo docs).

tools.name: ShipStation
tools.why: Standard multichannel shipping app from $14.99/month; 100,000+ businesses use its APIs (ShipStation docs; Ringly 2026 comparison). Official MCP repo exists.

tools.name: Etsy
tools.why: One of the four marketplaces (with eBay, TikTok Shop, Walmart) sellers most often run beside their own store; Open API v3 plus a docs-only official MCP.

tools.name: Judge.me
tools.why: Most-installed reviews app on Shopify: 239k installs, ~10.8% of Shopify stores (Storecensus/dodropshipping 2026) and 31% of the 2,000 most popular Shopify stores (Shopify Community, Sep 2026 data). REST API v1 with public and private tokens for Shopify, WooCommerce and BigCommerce; no MCP.

tools.name: Recharge
tools.why: Incumbent Shopify subscription platform: 15-20k+ merchants, more Shopify subscription brands than the rest of the category combined, and it bought Skio in April 2026 (Loopwork and digitalheroes 2026 comparisons). REST API (2021-11) for subscriptions, charges, addresses, webhooks; no official MCP.

tools.name: Matrixify
tools.why: The standard Shopify bulk import/export and store-migration app (4.9 stars, 1,700+ reviews; 'deepest CSV tool in the category' per productupload 2026); Excel/CSV/Google Sheets for 20 entity types up to 20 GB, and an official Matrixify MCP server.

tools.name: Salesforce Commerce Cloud
tools.why: Enterprise platform with only ~5.5k live stores but ~7% share of $50M-200M GMV merchants, and it took 320 of Adobe Commerce's departing stores in Q1 2026 (elogic 2026). Official Apache-2.0 B2C CLI, MCP and agent skills (~600 API operations).

tools.name: Adyen
tools.why: Third in payment management behind Stripe and PayPal (8.59% vs 34.5% and 30%, 6sense 2026) and the usual PSP for enterprise and omnichannel retail; Sessions/Advanced flow, Drop-in and platform plugins; official MIT adyen-mcp.

tools.name: Klarna
tools.why: Highest BNPL adoption among merchants (38%, ahead of Afterpay; 6sense via hostmerchantservices 2026); offered through Stripe, Adyen, Shopify and direct, with on-site messaging and express checkout.

tools.name: AfterShip
tools.why: One of the three returns and post-purchase leaders (with Loop Returns and Narvar) and the one vendor covering both tracking and returns across platforms (Ringly, Clickpost 2026 reviews).
